mainTopic: Procedures of the סוטה at the Eastern Gate, why two סוטות do not drink together, and uncovering her versus the stoned woman
overview: The גמרא explains that the סוטה is brought up and down on purpose to tire her out so she will confess, just as בית דין moves witnesses around to unsettle false testimony. It then asks why the משנה lists the יולדת at the Eastern Gate. It answers that a person must stand over their own קרבן, and that the תנא named one example out of a larger group. Next, a ברייתא rules that two סוטות do not drink together. The תנא קמא, identified as רבי שמעון, gives the reason as boldness, while רבי יהודה learns it from the word אותה. The practical difference is a trembling woman, and the rule against doing מצוות in bundles is resolved by having two כהנים. The גמרא then gives the source in the פסוק for uncovering the סוטה and unbraiding her hair. Finally, it reconciles רבי יהודה's views on the סוטה and on a woman being stoned, and רבא raises the same question about the רבנן and then begins resolving both, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: She is already standing there
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: why does the משנה say they bring her up to the Eastern Gate, if she is already standing there in the Temple, where the בית דין הגדול sits?
steps.simpleTranslation: She is already standing there!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the משנה. If the סוטה is already in the Temple area where the court sits, why describe bringing her up?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the סוטה is first brought to the בית דין הגדול and then brought up to the Eastern Gate. But the בית דין הגדול sits in the Temple area, so she is already there. Bringing her up to the gate seems pointless.

phrases.english: She is already standing there!
phrases.notes: He means she is already in the Temple area where the בית דין הגדול sits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's description of bringing the סוטה up to the Eastern Gate, when she is already in the Temple where the court sits.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that, after the בית דין הגדול, the סוטה is brought up to the Eastern Gate
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: She is already there, so moving her there seems to serve no purpose.

steps.title: They move her around to tire her out
steps.stepSummary: The movement up and down is done on purpose, to wear her down so she will confess.
steps.simpleTranslation: They would bring her up and bring her down in order to tire her out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The moving back and forth is deliberate; it is meant to exhaust her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goal is not to get her to a new place. The goal is to tire her so that, if she is guilty, she will admit it and not drink the water.

phrases.english: That we bring her up and we bring her down
in order to tire her out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the purpose of the action
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Bringing her up seemed pointless because she was already there.
steps.terutzMaskana: The movement has a purpose: to tire her out and push her to confess.

steps.title: The same tactic is used with witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר teaches that בית דין moves witnesses from place to place to unsettle them.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: The court moves the witnesses from place to place, so that their minds become unsettled and they take back their testimony.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that בית דין uses the same method with witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the witnesses are lying, moving them around confuses them and may lead them to retract. This supports the idea that the סוטה is moved around for a similar reason.

keyTerms.meaning: So that their minds become unsettled
And they will take back (their words)

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
The court moves the witnesses
from place to place,
so that their minds become unsettled
phrases.notes: This is about witnesses in a capital case, where a lie could cost a life.

phrases.english: and they will retract.

steps.whatToRemember: The סוטה is moved up and down on purpose to tire her into confessing, just as בית דין moves witnesses around to unsettle false testimony.
steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 2 with a parallel practice.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that בית דין deliberately moves people around to bring out the truth
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר about moving witnesses

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about the Eastern Gate
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: there they give the סוטות to drink, and so on.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: For there they give the סוטות to drink, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. This step sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the Eastern Gate is where סוטות drink, where מצורעים are purified, and where a יולדת is purified. The גמרא will now ask about each item on this list.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc.; the rest of the quote

phrases.english: For there they give the sota women to drink, etc.
phrases.notes: "There" means the Eastern Gate. The rest of the משנה line also mentions מצורעים and the יולדת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Eastern Gate is the place for giving the סוטה the water and for purifying מצורעים and the יולדת.

steps.title: Why does the יולדת stand at the gate?
steps.stepSummary: סוטות and מצורעים have a פסוק requiring them to stand "before ה׳", but what is the reason for the יולדת?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for סוטות, since it is written: "And the priest shall stand the woman before ה׳." It also makes sense for מצורעים, since it is written: "And the priest who purifies shall stand..." But what is the reason for a יולדת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the source for two items on the list but asks for the source of the third, the יולדת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Eastern Gate faces the Sanctuary, so it counts as "before ה׳". סוטה and מצורע each have a פסוק that uses this phrase. The יולדת has no such פסוק, so why is she listed?

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who has given birth

phrases.english: Granted for sota women, as it is written:
"And the priest shall stand the woman before the Lord,"
lepers too, as it is written:
"And the priest who purifies shall stand, etc.,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:11. The part not quoted ends with "before the Lord."

phrases.english: but a woman who gave birth, what is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the third item in the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the יולדת must stand at the Eastern Gate, when no פסוק says she stands "before ה׳"

steps.title: Because a person must stand over their own קרבן
steps.stepSummary: Suggested answer: the יולדת comes to stand by her קרבנות, since a person's קרבן is offered only while they stand over it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because they come and stand over their קרבנות, as it is taught: A person's קרבן is offered only if he stands over it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a reason for the יולדת: she must be present while her קרבן is offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא teaches that the owner must stand by their קרבן while it is offered. The יולדת is still impure and cannot enter, so she stands at the Eastern Gate, the closest place she may stand.

phrases.english: If you say it is because they come
and stand over their offerings,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: אֵין קׇרְבָּנוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם קָרֵב
phrases.english: as it is taught: A person's offering is not sacrificed

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן עוֹמֵד עַל גַּבָּיו.
phrases.english: unless he stands over it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to the question in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The יולדת stands at the Eastern Gate because a person must stand by their own קרבן while it is offered.
steps.confusionAlert: The word אילימא often opens an answer that gets rejected. Here it gets challenged, but in the end the גמרא keeps it.

steps.title: Then זבין and זבות should be listed too
steps.stepSummary: If the reason is standing over a קרבן, then זבים and זבות, who also bring קרבנות while impure, should also be listed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, זבין and זבות should be included as well!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. The reason seems too broad for a list that names only the יולדת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זבים and זבות also bring קרבנות to complete their purification. If the reason were simply standing by one's קרבן, the משנה should have named them too.

keyTerms.meaning: Men and women impure because of a bodily discharge

phrases.english: If so, zavim and zavot as well!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason that the יולדת stands at the gate to be present at her קרבן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same reason applies to זבים and זבות, yet the משנה does not list them.

steps.title: The תנא listed only one example
steps.stepSummary: Yes, זבים and זבות stand there too; the תנא simply mentioned one of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is indeed so, and the תנא mentioned just one of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge's point and keeps the answer. The משנה's list was not meant to be complete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone who brings a קרבן while impure stands at the Eastern Gate. The יולדת is just a sample of the whole group.

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so,
and the tanna cited one of them.

steps.whatToRemember: The יולדת stands at the Eastern Gate to be present at her קרבן. זבים and זבות do the same; the משנה just gave one example.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 by agreeing with it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the point; the list is only an example
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Naming only the יולדת seemed to exclude זבים and זבות.
steps.terutzMaskana: זבים and זבות are included too; the תנא mentioned only one case.

steps.title: Two סוטות do not drink together
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that two סוטות may not drink at the same time, so that one does not draw boldness from the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Two סוטות are not given to drink at the same time, so that one's heart does not become bold because of her friend.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא with a new rule: each סוטה drinks on her own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern is psychological. If one woman sees the other refuse to confess, she may also stay quiet, even if she is guilty.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: They do not give to drink
two sota women at once,

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא לִבָּהּ גַּס בַּחֲבֶירְתָּהּ.
phrases.english: so that her heart will not be emboldened by her friend.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן אֵין מַשְׁקִין שְׁתֵּי סוֹטוֹת כְּאַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic connected to giving the סוטה the water.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two סוטות are not given the water together, so that neither is emboldened by the other.

steps.title: רבי יהודה learns it from the word אותה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה agrees with the rule but says it comes from the פסוק: "אותה" means her alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: That is not the reason. Rather, the פסוק says "אותה", her, which means her alone.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives a different source for the same rule. For him it is a Torah law learned from a word in the פסוק, not a psychological concern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sides agree on the practical rule but disagree about why. The first view bases it on a worry about boldness. רבי יהודה reads "אותה" as limiting the process to one woman at a time.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not for that reason

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
This is not for that reason,
rather, the verse states:
"Her" — her alone.

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees that two סוטות do not drink together. The disagreement is only about the reason: a worry that one emboldens the other, or a word in the פסוק (רבי יהודה).
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה does not argue with the rule itself. He only rejects the reason and gives a different source for it.
steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר לֹא מִן הַשֵּׁם הוּא זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reason given in step 9 and replaces it with a source from a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule that two סוטות do not drink together comes from the word "אותה" in the פסוק.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the reason, not the rule
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rule comes from the פסוק itself, not from a psychological concern.

steps.title: How does the first opinion deal with the word 'her'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the תנא קמא can rely on logic alone when the פסוק says אותה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the first תנא: isn't it written 'her'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the תנא קמא a question. The תורה writes אותה, which רבי יהודה used as the source, so why does the תנא קמא give a reason instead of using the פסוק?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10, רבי יהודה said the rule comes from the word אותה. That makes it look as if the תנא קמא is ignoring a clear word in the פסוק. The גמרא wants to know how the תנא קמא reads that word.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה
'Her', the word in the פסוק that רבי יהודה reads as 'her alone'

phrases.english: And the first tanna,
isn't it written "her"?
phrases.notes: This is the same word רבי יהודה used in the previous step to prove that she drinks alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תנא קמא of step 9 using the פסוק that רבי יהודה cited in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The תנא קמא's logical reason (boldness) for the rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק explicitly says אותה. That seems to make the rule a plain decree of the תורה, so there is no need for a reason, and a reason alone seems to ignore the word.

steps.title: The first opinion is רבי שמעון, who explains the reason behind the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא is רבי שמעון. He agrees with אותה but explains why the תורה said it: so she does not draw boldness from the other woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first תנא is רבי שמעון, who explains the reasons behind פסוקים. He is saying: what is the reason the תורה said 'her' alone? So that her heart does not become bold because of her friend.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the תנא קמא does accept the word אותה. He is רבי שמעון, and he is simply giving the reason why the תורה wrote it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that the פסוק says 'her alone.' The disagreement is whether we use the reason behind the פסוק. רבי שמעון says the reason is to keep her from feeling bold next to another woman. רבי יהודה treats it as a plain rule of the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: He explains, and applies, the reason behind a פסוק
Her heart is bold; she feels confident and stops being afraid
Her friend, meaning the other סוטה

phrases.english: The first tanna is Rabbi Shimon,
who expounds the reason of the verse,
and he is saying 'what is the reason':
phrases.notes: He means the תנא קמא's words in step 9 aren't ignoring the פסוק. They explain why the פסוק said it.

phrases.english: What is the reason for "her" alone?
So that her heart will not be
emboldened by her friend.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּא קַמָּא — רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא, דְּדָרֵישׁ טַעַם דִּקְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the author and reframes his words as the reason behind the פסוק, not a rejection of it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנא קמא seemed to ignore the word אותה and rely only on logic.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא קמא is רבי שמעון. He accepts אותה and explains its purpose: preventing boldness.

steps.title: What practical difference is there between the two views?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference it makes whether the rule comes from a reason or from the word of the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the two opinions ever lead to a different ruling. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both רבי שמעון and רבי יהודה agree that two סוטות do not drink together. The גמרא wants a case where the source of the rule actually changes the outcome.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the practical difference between the two opinions?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After showing that both opinions agree on the rule, the גמרא asks for a practical difference.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the reason-based view and the פסוק-based view rule differently.

steps.title: The difference is a trembling woman
steps.stepSummary: The practical difference is a woman who is already trembling with fear.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them: a trembling woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two views differ about a woman who is already trembling with fear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A trembling woman is clearly not getting bold from the other woman. So by רבי שמעון's reason she could drink together with another. רבי יהודה reads אותה as an absolute rule, so for him she still must drink alone.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who is trembling with fear

phrases.english: There is a difference between them: a trembling woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A trembling woman: רבי שמעון would allow her to drink with another, and רבי יהודה would not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a classic idea: when we follow the reason behind a פסוק, the law can change in a case where that reason does not apply.

steps.title: Even a trembling woman can't drink together, because מצוות aren't done in bundles
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: a trembling woman still cannot drink with another, because we do not do מצוות in bundles.
steps.simpleTranslation: And can a trembling woman be given to drink together with another? But we do not do מצוות in bundles!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 14. There is a separate rule that blocks two סוטות from drinking at once, even when the boldness reason does not apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if רבי שמעון's boldness reason does not apply to a trembling woman, another principle still forbids it: doing several מצוות together as one bundle. If so, there seems to be no practical difference between רבי שמעון and רבי יהודה after all.

keyTerms.meaning: Give to drink, here the bitter water of the סוטה
But isn't it so that... (introduces a challenge)
In bundles, doing several מצוות together as one package

phrases.english: And a trembling woman, do we give her to drink with another?
But we do not perform
מצוות in bundles.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרוֹתֶתֶת מִי מַשְׁקִין? וְהָא אֵין עוֹשִׂין מִצְוֹת חֲבִילוֹת חֲבִילוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the practical difference proposed in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי שמעון would let a trembling woman drink together with another סוטה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A separate, general rule forbids doing מצוות in bundles. So two סוטות can never drink together, even if the boldness reason is missing.
steps.confusionAlert: This is a new and separate reason from boldness. Even if the boldness reason falls away, this 'bundles' rule could still forbid two women drinking together.

steps.title: The source: four מצוות that are not done two at a time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a source that lists four cases done one at a time because we do not do מצוות in bundles.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: we do not give two סוטות to drink at once, we do not purify two מצורעים at once, we do not pierce the ears of two slaves at once, and we do not break the necks of two calves at once, because we do not do מצוות in bundles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its challenge with a source. The source explicitly names סוטות as something done one at a time because of the 'bundles' rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source gives the 'bundles' rule as a general principle covering four different מצוות. Because סוטה is listed first, the rule applies to her no matter how she feels. That makes the challenge to step 14 strong.

keyTerms.meaning: People with צרעת, who go through a purification process
Piercing the ear, done to an עבד עברי who wants to stay with his master
Breaking the necks of calves, the עגלה ערופה ceremony

steps.whatToRemember: There are two reasons not to have two סוטות drink together: boldness (רבי שמעון) or the word אותה (רבי יהודה), plus a general rule against doing מצוות in bundles. The 'bundles' rule threatens the idea that a trembling woman makes a difference between the two views.

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: אֵין מַשְׁקִין שְׁתֵּי סוֹטוֹת כְּאַחַת,
phrases.english: As we learned: We do not give two sota women to drink at once,
and we do not purify two lepers at once,
and we do not pierce two slaves at once,
and we do not break the necks of two calves at once,
because we do not perform
מצוות in bundles.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: אֵין מַשְׁקִין שְׁתֵּי סוֹטוֹת כְּאַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for the 'bundles' principle cited in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: The challenge of step 15, that a trembling woman still may not drink with another.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A תנאי source listing סוטות, מצורעים, slaves and עגלות as never done two at once, because of the 'bundles' rule.

steps.title: One priest versus two priests
steps.stepSummary: אביי (or רב כהנא) resolves the contradiction. The rule against מצוות in bundles applies to one כהן, while רבי שמעון's case uses two כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said (some say it was רב כהנא): There is no contradiction. The source that forbids it is talking about one כהן. The source that allows it is talking about two כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from steps 15-16. Both sources can be true because they describe different setups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'we do not do מצוות in bundles' only stops one person from doing two מצוות at the same moment. If each of two כהנים gives one trembling woman to drink, nobody is bundling anything. So the practical difference from step 14 still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult: the two sources do not really contradict
Here... there: each source is talking about a different case

steps.whatToRemember: One כהן cannot give two סוטות to drink together. Two כהנים, each handling one woman, can. This keeps the practical difference of the trembling woman.

phrases.english: Abaye said, and some say it was Rav Kahana:
It is not difficult:
Here it is talking about one priest,
phrases.notes: This is the source from step 16 that forbids bundling מצוות.

phrases.english: there it is talking about two priests.
phrases.notes: This is רבי שמעון's case, where the trembling woman drinks along with another woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב כָּהֲנָא, לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in steps 15-16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (one כהן vs. two כהנים)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A trembling woman can never drink together with another woman, because we do not do מצוות in bundles.
steps.terutzMaskana: The bundling rule only applies to one כהן. With two כהנים, the trembling woman may drink alongside another.

steps.title: Source that the priest uncovers her body
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the כהן grabbing her clothes and brings a ברייתא. The extra word 'the woman' in the פסוק teaches that her body is uncovered too, not just her head.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And the כהן grabs her clothing.' The רבנן taught: 'And he shall uncover the woman's head.' From this I would only know her head. How do I know her body? Because the פסוק says 'the woman.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: the next line of the משנה. It brings the source in the פסוק for uncovering the סוטה's body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'her head' alone would only teach uncovering the head. The extra word 'הָאִשָּׁה' (the woman) is read as including her whole body. That is the source for the משנה's rule that the כהן pulls at her clothing.

phrases.english: And the priest grabs hold of her clothing.
The Rabbis taught:
"And he shall uncover the woman's head"
From this I only know about her head.
From where do we know about her body?
The verse says: "the woman."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The משנה's rule that the כהן uncovers the סוטה by grabbing her clothes.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading the word 'הָאִשָּׁה' in במדבר 5:18 as including her body.

steps.title: 'Her head' teaches unbraiding her hair
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks: if 'the woman' already includes everything, why say 'her head'? It answers that the כהן must also undo her braided hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the פסוק say 'and uncover her head'? It teaches that the כהן undoes her hair.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now deals with a problem its own reading creates. Once the whole woman is uncovered, the word 'head' looks extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If her whole body is uncovered, her head is uncovered too, so mentioning 'head' seems unnecessary. The ברייתא says the word teaches something more: the כהן does not just uncover her hair, he unbraids it.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your reading is right...)

phrases.english: If so, why does the verse say
"and uncover her head"?
phrases.notes: Once her whole body is uncovered, her head is obviously uncovered too, so why mention it?

phrases.english: It teaches that the priest unbraids her hair.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains a word that seems extra after step 18's reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: An extra word in the פסוק teaches a new detail
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The words 'her head' seem extra once the whole woman is uncovered.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Her head' teaches that the כהן unbraids her hair, not just uncovers it.

steps.title: Does רבי יהודה worry about improper thoughts?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's view that an attractive סוטה is not uncovered. It suggests that this means he worries about הרהור (improper thoughts) and the רבנן do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: If her heart was attractive... (he would not uncover it). Does this mean רבי יהודה worries about improper thoughts and the רבנן do not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה and draws a conclusion from it. This is a setup: the next step will attack that conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה does not uncover an attractive woman. That suggests he is concerned onlookers (like young כהנים) will have improper thoughts. The רבנן uncover every סוטה, which suggests they are not concerned.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say...? (drawing a conclusion)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אִם הָיָה לִבָּהּ וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: If her heart was... etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה continues: if her heart or hair was attractive, he would not uncover it.

phrases.english: Is this to say that Rabbi Yehuda
is concerned about improper thoughts,
and the Rabbis are not concerned?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the משנה and sets up a contradiction.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the argument between רבי יהודה and the רבנן is about worrying over הרהור.

steps.title: The stoning case shows the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges step 20 with a ברייתא about stoning. There רבי יהודה lets the woman be mostly uncovered, while the חכמים insist she stay clothed. So the opinions seem reversed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we have heard the opposite from them! As it is taught: A man is covered with one piece in front. A woman is covered with two pieces, one in front and one behind, because all of her is nakedness. These are the words of רבי יהודה. The חכמים say: A man is stoned naked, but a woman is not stoned naked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea from step 20. It quotes a ברייתא where רבי יהודה seems less worried about הרהור and the חכמים seem more worried.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At a stoning, רבי יהודה covers the woman only with two small pieces, so most of her body shows. That suggests he does not worry about הרהור. The חכמים say a woman is stoned fully clothed, which suggests they do worry. This is the reverse of what step 20 assumed.

keyTerms.meaning: Is stoned (put to death by stoning)

steps.confusionAlert: In the stoning case the opinions look reversed compared to the סוטה case. רבי יהודה is the more lenient one about uncovering, and the חכמים are the stricter one.

phrases.english: But we have heard the opposite from them,
as it is taught:
A man, they cover him
phrases.notes: This is talking about someone who is about to be stoned by בית דין.

phrases.english: with one piece in front of him,
and a woman with two pieces:
one in front of her and one behind her,
because all of her is nakedness,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
And the Sages say: A man is stoned naked,
but a woman is not stoned naked!
phrases.notes: So here the חכמים seem to be the ones worried about improper thoughts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the conclusion suggested in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רבי יהודה worries about הרהור and the רבנן do not.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא about stoning shows רבי יהודה letting a woman be mostly uncovered while the חכמים require her to be clothed. Their positions appear reversed.

steps.title: רבה explains why the two cases are different for רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers the contradiction in רבי יהודה's view. A סוטה might go home innocent and still be desired, but a woman being stoned is about to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: What is the reason here, by the סוטה? Perhaps she will leave the court innocent, and the young כהנים will be stirred up by her. There, by stoning, she is leaving the world.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה is answering the question from step 21: why does רבי יהודה protect the סוטה from being uncovered but not the woman being stoned?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה does worry about הרהור in both cases. The difference is what happens afterward. A סוטה may be found innocent and keep living, so the young כהנים who saw her could keep desiring her. The woman being stoned is about to die, so that worry disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: they will be provoked by her, stirred to desire her
she is departing, meaning she is about to die

phrases.english: Rabba said:
Here, what is the reason?
phrases.notes: "Here" means the סוטה case, where רבי יהודה says not to uncover an attractive woman.

phrases.english: Perhaps she will leave the court innocent,
and the young כהנים will be provoked by her.
There, she is departing.
phrases.notes: "There" is the stoning case. She is about to die, so nobody can chase after her later.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 21
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: the outcome afterward (she lives or she dies) changes whether the worry applies
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה seemed to worry about הרהור by the סוטה but ignore it by stoning
steps.terutzMaskana: He worries in both cases, but only when the woman will go on living can the desire cause real harm

steps.title: Objection: maybe the onlookers will desire other women
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a possible objection: even if she dies, seeing her might stir the onlookers to desire other women.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: they will come to be provoked by other women.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא imagines someone attacking רבה's answer, and it sets up a reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection says her death should not matter. Seeing an uncovered woman could still stir desire that the onlookers then turn toward other women. If so, the stoning case should also need covering.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you would say (introduces a possible objection)

phrases.english: And if you would say:
they will come to be provoked by other women

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction רבה just made
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that her death removes the worry
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Desire stirred by seeing her could carry over to other women, so her death should not solve the problem

steps.title: רבא's tradition: desire only works on what the eyes see
steps.stepSummary: The objection is rejected with רבא's tradition that the יצר הרע only controls what a person actually sees.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבא say: We have a tradition that the יצר הרע only controls what a person's eyes see.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection from step 23 and saves רבה's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Desire attaches to the woman a person actually saw. It does not spread to other women he did not see. Once the woman who was seen is gone, the danger is gone too.

keyTerms.meaning: we have it as a tradition

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבה (step 22) and רבא (here and the next steps). They are two different אמוראים whose names look almost the same.

phrases.english: But didn't Rava say:
It is learned by tradition that the evil inclination does not control
except over what his eyes see.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 23
steps.terutzResolutionType: A received tradition about how desire works
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Seeing one woman might stir desire for other women
steps.terutzMaskana: Desire only attaches to what is actually seen, so once she dies the worry ends
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יהודה: by a סוטה, who may live on, we worry about הרהור. By stoning, she dies, and desire only attaches to what the eyes see, so there is no worry.

steps.title: רבא: the Rabbis also seem to contradict themselves
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks why the גמרא only pointed out רבי יהודה's contradiction. The רבנן also seem to contradict themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Is only the contradiction of רבי יהודה against רבי יהודה difficult, while the contradiction of the רבנן against the רבנן is not difficult?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new problem: the רבנן's two rulings also seem to clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By a סוטה, the רבנן say to uncover her and do not worry about הרהור. By stoning, they insist she stay clothed, which looks like they do worry. So the same question that hit רבי יהודה hits them too.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Is the contradiction of Rabbi Yehuda against Rabbi Yehuda difficult,
while that of the Rabbis against the Rabbis is not difficult?
phrases.notes: The רבנן uncover the סוטה but keep the stoned woman covered. That looks just as inconsistent.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה קַשְׁיָא, דְּרַבָּנַן אַדְּרַבָּנַן לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי יהודה's contradiction to the parallel contradiction in the רבנן
steps.kashyaTarget: The two rulings of the רבנן (סוטה versus stoning)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן ignore הרהור by the סוטה but seem to care about it by stoning

steps.title: רבא agrees רבי יהודה is already settled
steps.stepSummary: רבא rephrases his point. רבי יהודה's contradiction is already answered, and he goes on (on the next amud) to show that the רבנן are not difficult either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: The contradiction of רבי יהודה against רבי יהודה is not difficult, as we answered.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא confirms that רבי יהודה's view is resolved by רבה's answer. This sets up the next move, which is explaining the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא fixes how his question should be put. רבי יהודה needs no new answer, because the explanation in steps 22 to 24 already works. רבא then goes on to explain that the רבנן's two rulings do not contradict each other either; that comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא קַשְׁיָא,
phrases.english: The contradiction of Rabbi Yehuda against Rabbi Yehuda is not difficult,
as we answered.
phrases.notes: This points back to רבה's answer in step 22: the סוטה may live on, but the stoned woman dies.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא withdraws his question and begins resolving both contradictions, starting with רבי יהודה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Confirms the earlier answer for רבי יהודה and narrows the open problem
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both רבי יהודה and the רבנן seemed to need answers
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה is already answered; the remaining question is about the רבנן
